chunks: And in the narration of Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Ala' from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

It concerns a man whom another man entrusts with thirty dirhams to buy a garment, and another [man] entrusts him with twenty dirhams for a garment. So he sent the two garments, but this one did not know his garment, nor did that one know his garment. He [the Imam] said: "The two garments are sold, and the owner of the thirty is given three-fifths of the price, and the other is given two-fifths of the price." I said: "What if the owner of the twenty said to the owner of the thirty, 'Choose whichever you wish'?" He [the Imam] said: "He has treated him fairly."
ai.seo_question: How are proceeds divided when two indistinguishable items are bought with different amounts of money?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* illustrates the principle of proportional division (*nisab*) in cases of commingled assets where individual identification is lost, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on equitable compensation based on capital contribution. The Imam’s validation of the voluntary choice by the smaller contributor highlights the interplay between strict legal entitlement (*haqq*) and voluntary generosity (*ihsan*) in commercial transactions. This case serves as a foundational precedent for modern Islamic finance regarding the distribution of mixed funds or goods.
